title: git pull --rebase refuses to run with uncommitted changes unless rebase.autoStash is set
body: `git pull --rebase` aborts with 'cannot pull with rebase: You have unstaged changes'. Either commit or stash first, or set `git config --global rebase.autoStash true` so git stashes, rebases and re-applies the changes automatically. Conflicts while re-applying leave the stash in place.

title: Git on Windows rewrites LF to CRLF and makes shell scripts fail in Linux containers
body: With `core.autocrlf=true` a checkout on Windows converts `.sh` files to CRLF; copied into a Linux image they fail with `/bin/bash^M: bad interpreter`. Add a `.gitattributes` with `*.sh text eol=lf` and renormalize with `git add --renormalize .`.

title: Git submodules are checked out in detached HEAD so commits made inside them are easy to lose
body: `git submodule update` checks out the commit recorded by the superproject, not a branch. Commits made there belong to no branch and disappear on the next update. Run `git switch -c work` inside the submodule before committing, push it, then `git add <submodule>` in the superproject.

title: Docker rebuilds every dependency layer because COPY . . comes before the install step
body: Any source change invalidates the cache for every instruction after `COPY . .`. Copy only the manifest first (`COPY package.json package-lock.json ./`), run `npm ci`, then copy the rest. Dependency layers are then reused until the lockfile changes.

title: A container cannot reach a service on the host through localhost
body: Inside a container `localhost` is the container itself. On Docker Desktop use `host.docker.internal`; on Linux add `--add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway` or run with `--network host`. The host service must also listen on 0.0.0.0, not 127.0.0.1, when not using host networking.

title: Container ignores SIGTERM and takes 10 seconds to stop because the app runs as PID 1 under a shell
body: With shell-form `CMD npm start` the shell is PID 1 and does not forward SIGTERM, so `docker stop` waits for the timeout and SIGKILLs. Use exec form `CMD ["node", "server.js"]`, or add `--init` / tini so signals reach the process and zombies are reaped.

title: PostgreSQL connections stuck idle in transaction hold locks and block migrations
body: A session that opened a transaction and never committed shows `idle in transaction` in `pg_stat_activity` and keeps its row and table locks, so an `ALTER TABLE` waits forever. Find them by state and `xact_start`, terminate with `pg_terminate_backend(pid)`, and set `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout` to prevent it.

title: PostgreSQL ignores the index when the query filters on lower(email)
body: A plain B-tree index on `email` cannot serve `WHERE lower(email) = $1`. Create an expression index `CREATE INDEX ON users (lower(email))` or use the `citext` type. Check with `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` that the plan switches from Seq Scan to Index Scan.

title: Inserts fail with duplicate key after restoring PostgreSQL data because the sequence was not advanced
body: Loading rows with explicit ids leaves the serial sequence at its old value, so the next insert reuses an existing id. Fix with `SELECT setval(pg_get_serial_sequence('orders','id'), max(id)) FROM orders;`. pg_dump handles this automatically; manual CSV imports do not.

title: SQLite database is locked errors disappear after switching to WAL journal mode
body: In the default rollback journal a writer blocks all readers. `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` lets readers proceed during a write; combine it with `PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000` so a second writer waits instead of failing immediately. WAL needs the -wal and -shm files next to the database and does not work on network filesystems.

title: Using KEYS in production Redis blocks the server for seconds
body: `KEYS pattern` scans the whole keyspace in a single blocking call. Use `SCAN` with `MATCH` and `COUNT` and iterate the cursor until it returns 0; it is incremental and lets other clients run in between. The same applies to `SMEMBERS` on huge sets (use `SSCAN`).

title: Python function default list is shared between calls and accumulates values
body: Default arguments are evaluated once at definition time, so `def add(x, items=[])` keeps appending to the same list across calls. Use `items=None` and create the list inside the function. Linters flag this as B006.

title: pip installs packages outside the virtualenv because a different pip is first on PATH
body: Running `pip install` after activating a venv can still hit the system pip when PATH is ordered differently or the shell caches the command. Always call `python -m pip install ...` with the venv interpreter, and check `python -m pip --version` shows the venv path.

title: A blocking call inside an asyncio coroutine freezes every other task
body: `time.sleep`, `requests.get` or heavy CPU work inside `async def` blocks the event loop thread. Use `await asyncio.sleep`, an async client like httpx, or offload with `await asyncio.to_thread(fn)`. Enable `PYTHONASYNCIODEBUG=1` to log slow callbacks.

title: Comparing naive and timezone-aware datetimes raises TypeError in Python
body: `datetime.now()` is naive while values parsed from ISO strings with an offset are aware, and comparing them raises `can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes`. Use `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` everywhere and store UTC; convert to local time only for display.

title: require() of an ES module fails with ERR_REQUIRE_ESM after a dependency upgrade
body: Packages that switched to ESM-only (for example node-fetch 3, chalk 5) cannot be loaded with `require`. Either convert the project to ESM (`"type": "module"`), use dynamic `await import()`, or pin the last CommonJS major version.

title: Node process exits on an unhandled promise rejection since Node 15
body: An async function that throws without a `catch` now terminates the process instead of printing a warning. Add error handling to every promise chain, and register `process.on('unhandledRejection', ...)` only for logging, not as a substitute.

title: npm ci fails because package-lock.json is out of sync with package.json
body: `npm ci` refuses to install when the lockfile does not match the manifest, which is the point: CI must be reproducible. Run `npm install` locally to regenerate the lockfile, commit it, and never edit dependencies in package.json without updating the lock.

title: Enabling strictNullChecks in TypeScript surfaces hundreds of possibly undefined errors
body: With `strict` on, values typed `T | undefined` must be narrowed before use. Migrate file by file: narrow with guards or optional chaining, avoid sprinkling non-null assertions (`!`), and type API responses so undefined is explicit at the boundary.

title: React useEffect runs in an infinite loop because an object dependency is recreated every render
body: An object or array literal in the dependency list is a new reference on each render, so the effect fires, sets state, re-renders and fires again. Depend on primitive fields, memoize with `useMemo`/`useCallback`, or move the value inside the effect.

title: React StrictMode runs effects twice in development and makes API calls fire twice
body: In React 18 development builds StrictMode mounts, unmounts and remounts components to expose missing cleanup. It does not happen in production. Return a cleanup function (abort controller, unsubscribe) instead of removing StrictMode.

title: Flex child with long text overflows its container instead of shrinking
body: Flex items default to `min-width: auto`, so they never shrink below their content width and long words or code blocks overflow. Set `min-width: 0` on the flex child (or `overflow: hidden`) so `text-overflow: ellipsis` and wrapping work.

title: CORS preflight fails when the browser sends credentials and the server answers Access-Control-Allow-Origin *
body: With `credentials: 'include'` the wildcard origin is rejected. The server must echo the exact Origin, send `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, and answer the OPTIONS preflight with the allowed methods and headers before auth middleware runs.

title: Intermittent 502 from the load balancer because the app keep-alive timeout is shorter than the LB idle timeout
body: If the Node or Go server closes idle connections before the load balancer does, the LB reuses a socket the server just closed and returns 502. Set the server keep-alive timeout above the LB idle timeout (for example 65 s against an AWS ALB at 60 s).

title: TLS works in the browser but curl and Java fail with unable to get local issuer certificate
body: The server sends only the leaf certificate; browsers fetch the missing intermediate themselves, other clients do not. Serve the full chain (leaf plus intermediates, e.g. fullchain.pem) and verify with `openssl s_client -connect host:443 -showcerts`.

title: Kubernetes pod in CrashLoopBackOff because the liveness probe kills it during slow startup
body: A liveness probe that starts checking before the app is ready restarts the container in a loop. Add a `startupProbe` with a generous `failureThreshold * periodSeconds`, keep liveness for deadlocks only, and use readiness to gate traffic.

title: Pod restarts with OOMKilled although the JVM heap is below the container limit
body: Heap is only part of JVM memory: metaspace, thread stacks and direct buffers count too. Size the heap as a percentage with `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75`, leave headroom, and check `kubectl describe pod` for `Last State: OOMKilled`.

title: Changing a Kubernetes ConfigMap does not update environment variables in running pods
body: Values injected with `env`/`envFrom` are read only at container start. Mounted ConfigMap volumes update eventually, env vars never. Trigger a rollout (`kubectl rollout restart deployment/x`) or add a checksum annotation of the config to the pod template.

title: Bash script keeps going after a failed command inside a pipeline despite set -e
body: `set -e` only looks at the exit status of the last command of a pipeline, so `false | tee log` succeeds. Add `set -o pipefail` (usually `set -euo pipefail`). Also note that a failing command substitution inside `local x=$(cmd)` is masked by `local`.

title: Unquoted variable in bash breaks on file names with spaces
body: `rm $file` splits the value on whitespace and expands globs, so 'my file.txt' becomes two arguments. Always quote expansions (`"$file"`, `"$@"`) and run shellcheck, which reports this as SC2086.

title: Windows build fails with file not found because the path exceeds 260 characters
body: Deep node_modules or build trees hit MAX_PATH. Enable long paths (`LongPathsEnabled` registry key and `git config --global core.longpaths true`) or build from a short directory such as C:\src. Some older tools still ignore the setting.

title: PowerShell refuses to run a local script because running scripts is disabled on this system
body: The default execution policy on client Windows is Restricted. Use `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned` for your user, or run a single script with `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File script.ps1`. Downloaded files may also need `Unblock-File`.

title: CMake keeps using an old compiler or option after changing it because CMakeCache.txt is stale
body: Cached variables such as CMAKE_C_COMPILER or option() values are only read on first configure. Changing the toolchain requires deleting the build directory (or `cmake --fresh` on 3.24+); passing -D again overrides options but not the compiler.

title: strncpy does not NUL-terminate the destination when the source is too long
body: `strncpy(dst, src, sizeof dst)` fills the buffer without a terminator if src is longer, and later reads run off the end. Use `snprintf(dst, sizeof dst, "%s", src)` and check the return value for truncation, or strlcpy where available.

title: Goroutines started in a loop all see the last value of the loop variable before Go 1.22
body: Before Go 1.22 the loop variable was shared across iterations, so `go func(){ use(v) }()` read whatever value v had when the goroutine ran. Pass it as an argument or shadow it (`v := v`); Go 1.22 makes each iteration a new variable.

title: A Go error interface holding a nil pointer is not equal to nil
body: Returning a typed nil pointer (`var e *MyErr = nil; return e`) as `error` produces a non-nil interface with a nil value, so `err != nil` is true. Return a literal `nil` on success paths.

title: Rust rejects modifying a Vec while iterating over it with cannot borrow as mutable
body: Iterating with `for x in &v` holds an immutable borrow, so `v.push` inside the loop fails to compile. Collect changes and apply them after the loop, iterate over indices, or use `retain` / `drain_filter`-style APIs.

title: Objects used as HashMap keys are not found because equals was overridden without hashCode
body: HashMap first compares hash codes; two equal objects with different default hashCode values land in different buckets. Always override both together (or use records / Lombok @EqualsAndHashCode) and keep key fields immutable.

title: Spring @Transactional is ignored when the method is called from the same class
body: Transactions are applied by a proxy, and a call through `this` bypasses it, so no transaction starts and no rollback happens. Move the method to another bean, inject self, or use TransactionTemplate.

title: LazyInitializationException when serializing a JPA entity to JSON outside the transaction
body: Lazy associations are loaded on access; once the session is closed, Jackson touching them throws `could not initialize proxy - no Session`. Map to DTOs inside the service, fetch what you need with a join fetch or entity graph, and keep open-in-view disabled.

title: Flutter setState called after dispose when an async call finishes after leaving the screen
body: A Future that completes after the widget is removed calls setState on a defunct State and logs an error. Check `if (!mounted) return;` after every await, and cancel streams and timers in dispose.

title: GitHub Actions cache from a feature branch is not visible to other branches
body: Caches are scoped: a run can restore caches from its own branch and the default branch, not from sibling branches. Warm the cache on the default branch, or accept a cold first run per branch; pull requests can read caches of their base branch.

title: GitHub Actions secrets are empty in pull requests opened from forks
body: Workflows triggered by `pull_request` from a fork run without repository secrets and with a read-only token, so deploy or signing steps fail. Keep those steps on push to protected branches; `pull_request_target` exposes secrets and must never check out and run untrusted fork code.

title: git clone over SSH inside a remote server fails with permission denied publickey
body: The key lives on your laptop, not on the server. Either forward the agent (`ssh -A` or `ForwardAgent yes` for that host only) or use a deploy key on the server. Check with `ssh -T git@github.com` and `ssh-add -l`.

title: JWT validation fails with token not yet valid because the server clock is skewed
body: An `nbf` or `iat` slightly in the future is rejected when the verifier's clock lags the issuer. Keep clocks synced with NTP/chrony and allow a small leeway (30-60 seconds) in the JWT library.

title: JSON parser fails with unexpected token at position 0 on a file saved by Windows tools
body: Some Windows editors and PowerShell 5 `Out-File` write a UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF) that strict JSON parsers reject. Save as UTF-8 without BOM, or strip it before parsing (`text.lstrip('\ufeff')`).

title: Money totals are off by a cent because amounts are stored as floating point
body: Binary floats cannot represent 0.1 exactly, so sums drift (0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004). Store money as integer minor units or a decimal type (NUMERIC in SQL, BigDecimal, Python Decimal) and round only at presentation.

title: A regular expression with nested quantifiers hangs the service on some inputs
body: Patterns like `(a+)+$` backtrack exponentially on near-matching input (ReDoS). Remove nested quantifiers, anchor patterns, use possessive/atomic groups, or switch to a linear-time engine such as RE2 for untrusted input.

title: Scheduled cron job runs an hour off after the daylight saving change
body: The scheduler interprets the expression in the host or container time zone, often UTC, while the business expects local time. Set the scheduler time zone explicitly (CRON_TZ, Kubernetes CronJob `timeZone`) or schedule in UTC and document it.

title: Server disk fills up because an application log file is never rotated
body: A process writing to a single file grows it forever; deleting the file while it is open does not free space until the process closes it (check `lsof +L1`). Configure logrotate with copytruncate or a reopen signal, or log to stdout and let the platform rotate.
